text:
Brayden McNabb is 35, an original Golden Knight with a 2023 Stanley Cup ring, and Vegas still hands him a little over 20 minutes a night. He has no goals in 25 games and nine assists, one of them in his last ten. Offense was never the job.

The job is keeping the puck out of his net, and it is getting done. Vegas takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly six points better than without him. The team has also scored 3.6 fewer goals than those chances deserve during his shifts, so the results undersell the play.

None of this is new. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.17 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there last season (91st percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%. His ice time is up about two minutes a night over his last ten games. The thing to watch: his top speed sits in the 5th percentile by NHL EDGE, so positioning has to keep doing the work.
